nested, indent, sort_keys, ensure_ascii with unicode, separators, custom default/cls).

1	from __future__ import annotations
2	
3	import json
4	import os
5	import tempfile
6	from collections.abc import Callable, Generator
7	from datetime import date, datetime, time
8	from decimal import Decimal
9	from typing import Any
10	
11	from fsutil.args import get_path as _get_path
12	from fsutil.checks import assert_file, assert_not_dir, exists
13	from fsutil.deps import require_requests
14	from fsutil.operations import make_dirs_for_file, remove_file
15	from fsutil.paths import split_filepath
16	from fsutil.perms import get_permissions, set_permissions
17	from fsutil.types import PathIn
18	
19	
20	def read_file(path: PathIn, encoding: str = "utf-8") -> str:
21	    """
22	    Read the content of the file at the given path using the specified encoding.
23	    """
24	    path = _get_path(path)
25	    assert_file(path)
26	    with open(path, encoding=encoding) as file:
27	        content = file.read()
28	    return content
29	
30	
31	def read_file_from_url(url: str, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
32	    """
33	    Read the content of the file at the given url.
34	    """
35	    requests = require_requests()
36	    response = requests.get(url, **kwargs)
37	    response.raise_for_status()
38	    content = str(response.text)
39	    return content
40	
41	
42	def read_file_json(
43	    path: PathIn,
44	    cls: type[json.JSONDecoder] | None = None,
45	    object_hook: Callable[[dict[Any, Any]], Any] | None = None,
46	    parse_float: Callable[[str], Any] | None = None,
47	    parse_int: Callable[[str], Any] | None = None,
48	    parse_constant: Callable[[str], Any] | None = None,
49	    object_pairs_hook: Callable[[list[tuple[Any, Any]]], Any] | None = None,
50	    *,
51	    encoding: str = "utf-8",
52	    **kwargs: Any,
53	) -> Any:
54	    """
55	    Read and decode a json encoded file at the given path.
56	    All the decoding options supported by ``json.loads`` are accepted.
57	    """
58	    path = _get_path(path)
59	    content = read_file(path, encoding=encoding)
60	    data = json.loads(
61	        content,
62	        cls=cls,
63	        object_hook=object_hook,
64	        parse_float=parse_float,
65	        parse_int=parse_int,
66	        parse_constant=parse_constant,
67	        object_pairs_hook=object_pairs_hook,
68	        **kwargs,
69	    )
70	    return data
71	
72	
73	def _read_file_lines_in_range(
74	    path: PathIn,
75	    line_start: int = 0,
76	    line_end: int = -1,
77	    encoding: str = "utf-8",
78	) -> Generator[str, None, None]:
79	    path = _get_path(path)
80	    line_start_negative = line_start < 0
81	    line_end_negative = line_end < 0
82	    if line_start_negative or line_end_negative:
83	        # pre-calculate lines count only if using negative line indexes
84	        lines_count = read_file_lines_count(path)
85	        # normalize negative indexes
86	        if line_start_negative:
87	            line_start = max(0, line_start + lines_count)
88	        if line_end_negative:
89	            line_end = min(line_end + lines_count, lines_count - 1)
90	    with open(path, "rb") as file:
91	        file.seek(0)
92	        line_index = 0
93	        for line in file:
94	            if line_index >= line_start and line_index <= line_end:
95	                yield line.decode(encoding)
96	            line_index += 1
97	
98	
99	def read_file_lines(
100	    path: PathIn,
101	    line_start: int = 0,
102	    line_end: int = -1,
103	    strip_white: bool = True,
104	    skip_empty: bool = True,
105	    encoding: str = "utf-8",
106	) -> list[str]:
107	    """
108	    Read file content lines.
109	    It is possible to specify the line indexes (negative indexes too),
110	    very useful especially when reading large files.
111	    """
112	    path = _get_path(path)
113	    assert_file(path)
114	    if line_start == 0 and line_end == -1:
115	        content = read_file(path, encoding=encoding)
116	        lines = content.splitlines()
117	    else:
118	        # only the requested range is decoded, the file is streamed line by line.
119	        lines = list(
120	            _read_file_lines_in_range(
121	                path,
122	                line_start=line_start,
123	                line_end=line_end,
124	                encoding=encoding,
125	            )
126	        )
127	    if strip_white:
128	        lines = [line.strip() for line in lines]
129	    if skip_empty:
130	        lines = [line for line in lines if line]
131	    return lines
132	
133	
134	def read_file_lines_count(path: PathIn) -> int:
135	    """
136	    Read file lines count.
137	    """
138	    path = _get_path(path)
139	    assert_file(path)
140	    with open(path, "rb") as file:
141	        file.seek(0)
142	        lines_count = sum(1 for _ in file)
143	    return lines_count
144	
145	
146	def _get_default_file_permissions() -> int:
147	    """
148	    Get the permissions a newly created file would get, honoring the umask.
149	    """
150	    umask = os.umask(0)
151	    os.umask(umask)
152	    return 0o666 & ~umask
153	
154	
155	def _write_file_atomic(
156	    path: PathIn,
157	    content: str,
158	    append: bool = False,
159	    encoding: str = "utf-8",
160	) -> None:
161	    path = _get_path(path)
162	    if append and exists(path):
163	        content = read_file(path, encoding=encoding) + content
164	    dirpath, _ = split_filepath(path)
165	    temp_path = None
166	    try:
167	        # the content is fully written and flushed to a temporary file living in
168	        # the same directory (hence on the same filesystem), then moved over the
169	        # destination: readers either see the old or the new content, never both.
170	        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
171	            mode="w",
172	            dir=dirpath or os.curdir,
173	            delete=False,
174	            encoding=encoding,
175	        ) as file:
176	            file.write(content)
177	            file.flush()
178	            os.fsync(file.fileno())
179	            temp_path = file.name
180	        # file is now closed, safe to replace on Windows
181	        permissions = get_permissions(path) if exists(path) else None
182	        os.replace(temp_path, path)
183	        # temporary files are created private (0600), so the permissions of the
184	        # replaced file are restored, or the default ones are applied.
185	        if permissions is not None:
186	            set_permissions(path, permissions)
187	        else:
188	            os.chmod(path, _get_default_file_permissions())
189	    finally:
190	        # manually delete the temporary file if it still exists,
191	        # eg. if an error occurred before/during the replace.
192	        if temp_path and exists(temp_path):
193	            remove_file(temp_path)
194	
195	
196	def _write_file_non_atomic(
197	    path: PathIn,
198	    content: str,
199	    append: bool = False,
200	    encoding: str = "utf-8",
201	) -> None:
202	    path = _get_path(path)
203	    mode = "a" if append else "w"
204	    with open(path, mode, encoding=encoding) as file:
205	        file.write(content)
206	
207	
208	def write_file(
209	    path: PathIn,
210	    content: str,
211	    append: bool = False,
212	    encoding: str = "utf-8",
213	    atomic: bool = False,
214	) -> None:
215	    """
216	    Write file with the specified content at the given path.
217	    """
218	    path = _get_path(path)
219	    assert_not_dir(path)
220	    make_dirs_for_file(path)
221	    write_file_func = _write_file_atomic if atomic else _write_file_non_atomic
222	    write_file_func(
223	        path,
224	        content,
225	        append=append,
226	        encoding=encoding,
227	    )
228	
229	
230	def _json_default_encoder(obj: Any) -> Any:
231	    """
232	    Encode the objects that the json module doesn't know how to serialize.

132	    encoding: str = "utf-8",

138	    dirpath, _ = split_filepath(path)
